highlight.text: In it, he professes to define the principles of beauty and grace which he, a real child of Rococo, saw realized in serpentine lines (the Line of Beauty).

work.text: In 1745, Hogarth painted a self-portrait with his pug dog, Trump (now also in Tate Britain), which shows him as a learned artist supported by volumes of Shakespeare, Milton and Swift.
The portrait was originally created with the intention of Hogarth wearing formal attire, but was changed to the informal attire sometime during the painting process.

moment.text: there is drawn a waving line, with the words, " Line of Beauty " — a hieroglyphic of which no one could at first divine the meaning. The mystery was afterwards solved in his " Analysis of Beauty,"
